entries.title: Jeremiah 45:1
segments: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim; see

.  This prophecy belongs to an earlier date than those recorded in the preceding eight chapters. 
 
It is well to count before hand the cost of God's service, and to hold ourselves ready to endure hardships in the performance of it.  We ought never to set our hearts on personal ease and preferment; but in times of general public calamity this is peculiarly improper; we should then be content with the continuance of our lives, and our opportunities to labor in behalf of God's cause.

entries.title: Jeremiah 45:3
segments: Woe is me now; Baruch was dismayed in view of the sufferings to which he was exposed in consequence of writing the roll mentioned in
, as well as of the calamitous condition of his country.

entries.title: Jeremiah 45:5
segments: And seekest thou great things for thyself? in a time of general desolation, Baruch must not set his heart on temporal ease, honor, and affluence.
